rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however denominated, of more than one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.key_value: one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.exemptions: An advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed if the lease term is six months or longer. A landlord and tenant may agree, at the tenant's request and for a specified fee, to alterations other than cleaning or repairing. Certain small landlords may charge up to two months' rent (paragraph (5)). The subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This subdivision shall not apply to a security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.

rules.title: Small landlord security deposit cap of two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person, or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent, may not demand or receive security of more than two months' rent, in addition to the first month's rent.

rules.title: Service member higher security disclosure and return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard or advertised security due to credit history, credit score, housing history or another tenant factor, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason on or before lease signing. The additional amount must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.coverage_text: Service members renting residential property in which they will reside.
rules.quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

rules.title: Limits on deductions from security
rules.requirement: The landlord may claim from the security only amounts reasonably necessary for the listed purposes, and may not claim for conditions that preexisted the tenancy or for ordinary wear and tear.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: (A) The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.

rules.title: Initial move-out inspection notice
rules.requirement: Within a reasonable time after notice of intent to terminate, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection and the right to be present.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to subdivision (2), (3), or (4) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
rules.quoted_span: (f) (1) Within a reasonable time after notification of either party’s intention to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

rules.title: Photographs of unit for security deductions
rules.requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit after possession is returned and before repairs or cleanings that will be deducted, and again after they are completed; for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

rules.title: Return of security and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the security received and its disposition and return any remaining security to the tenant.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises

rules.exemptions: Supporting documentation under paragraphs (2) and (3) is not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived those rights, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 calendar days.
rules.penalty: The landlord shall not be entitled to claim any amount of the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with this subdivision.
